items.assessment: One SWAP kernel remains authoritative; F-TB07 adds testbank support only.
No kernel I/O or legacy adapter behavior changes.
The application-accuracy contract carries numerical policy/provenance, not physical state or forcing.
No persistent column state is added by the contract or testbank adoption.
No solver scratch ownership changes.
No storage-layout or batching changes.
The seam materializes numerical configuration before execution and cannot commit a rejected physical trial.
Checkpoint, retry and warm-start semantics are untouched.
No calendar unit or midnight assumption is introduced; the budget is interval-policy data.
No fixed coupling-window duration is introduced.
Coupling accuracy policy is explicit in the runtime/coupler contract rather than hidden in kernel physics.
Application head/drawdown accuracy remains separate from the hard H_SWAP=H_MF and q_SWAP=-q_MF interface contract; no production MODFLOW admission is claimed.
Water mass conservation is untouched, absolute and not traded against application accuracy.
Model-owned temporal-indicator transport remains explicit; interface-sensitivity outputs themselves are unchanged.
The contract adds no mandatory extra full SWAP trajectory.
No MultiSWAP state or worker architecture changes.
No MODFLOW-cell/tile mapping assumptions are added.
Deep-vadose remains an external optional component and is unaffected.
No component storage-transfer semantics change.
Alternative soil-water solver abstraction remains untouched.
No SWAP process physics is duplicated or altered.
The contract does not access HeadCalc internals; it targets the generic numerical-config carrier.
Externally qualified application accuracy remains numerical/application policy, explicitly separated from physical configuration.
No solver-cost, fallback or bounded-cost policy changes.
Reference-mode physics and numerical accuracy remain unchanged; current reference temporal-indicator normalization is only preserved.
Contract identity, provenance, qualification availability, head-domain budget and normalization are explicit and testable.
No optional per-column state or compute allocation is introduced.
Application/coupler policy remains outside kernel system-composition ownership.
No implicit file, path, midnight, one-day or direct-MODFLOW dependency is introduced.
The adoption is explicitly audited and requires exact-head CI without production-source change.
